title: Relational overview
subtitle: All 12 tables and all 16 foreign keys, with identity fields only.
notes: Use the Domain selector to view one area at a time. Dashed reference cards repeat an existing entity; all relationships appear once across the three views.
Crow's-foot markers show cardinalities at both ends. Dashed links are non-identifying: every child table has its own surrogate primary key.
A user may have zero or one student profile and zero or one recruiter profile. Role exclusivity is application logic, not a database inheritance relationship.
The two messages-to-users links are distinct: sender_id and receiver_id.

NULL labels follow the ORM model literally. A default value does not imply NOT NULL.
Only recruiter_id on internships and internship_id on interviews are nullable foreign keys.
student_skills, applications and saved_internships have surrogate IDs but no composite pair-uniqueness constraints.
documents belongs to students; there is no documents-to-applications foreign key. Application resume content is stored separately in applications.resume_url.

title: Actors and system responsibilities
subtitle: Student, recruiter and administrator goals inside the HireHub system boundary.
notes: The three role views are projections of the same HireHub system, not separate systems.
Actors remain outside the system boundary. Ellipses represent user goals; unarrowed solid lines show participation.
Authenticated access is a precondition for protected goals, not an include arrow to a login screen.
Messaging requires an existing application connection. Shared goal names appear for each participating role to keep the view readable.
Admin self-registration, email delivery, a calendar grid and machine-learned matching are not shown as implemented capabilities.

title: Submit an application
subtitle: Internal application request, optional resume, rejection paths and both commits.
code:
sequenceDiagram autonumber actor S as Student participant UI as React student UI participant API as FastAPI applications route participant DB as MySQL via SQLAlchemy S->>UI: Submit application with optional resume UI->>API: POST /api/applications (bearer token, multipart) API->>DB: Load account by token subject DB-->>API: Account identity API->>API: Check active-account flag API->>DB: Find student, internship, existing application DB-->>API: Related records and duplicate result alt Missing profile or internship API-->>UI: 404 response else Application already exists API-->>UI: 400 response else New application opt Resume supplied API->>API: Read resume bytes break Abort request if size exceeds 8 MiB API-->>UI: 413 response before writes end opt Non-empty file API->>API: Encode data URI and queue Document end end API->>DB: INSERT Application (+ optional Document), COMMIT 1 DB-->>API: Application ID, refreshed record API->>DB: INSERT student alert (+ recruiter alert if linked), COMMIT 2 DB-->>API: Alerts persisted API-->>UI: Application response with related internship UI-->>S: Confirmation, refresh listing/dashboard data end Note over API,DB: Application and alerts
use separate commits.
COMMIT 1 survives a later
alert failure.
Duplicate checks are not
a UNIQUE constraint.
notes: Solid arrows are requests/calls; dashed arrows are replies. opt and alt frames show conditional behavior.
Authentication/token rejection and database exceptions can terminate processing; the diagram details business validation branches after successful authentication.
COMMIT 1 saves the application and optional document. COMMIT 2 saves alerts. These boundaries intentionally match the current code.

title: Schedule an interview
subtitle: Recruiter scheduling with the current authorization and transaction behavior.
code:
sequenceDiagram autonumber actor R as Recruiter participant UI as ApplicantsView participant API as FastAPI recruiter route participant DB as MySQL via SQLAlchemy R->>UI: Select candidate, enter interview details UI->>API: POST /api/recruiter/interviews API->>DB: Load active account and recruiter profile DB-->>API: Recruiter identity Note over API,DB: Recruiter role is checked.
Candidate ownership
is not checked here. API->>DB: INSERT Interview, COMMIT 1, refresh DB-->>API: Saved interview API->>DB: Find Application by submitted application_id DB-->>API: Application record opt Referenced application found API->>API: Set status to Interview Scheduled API->>API: Queue student notification if student is linked API->>DB: UPDATE Application (+ notification), COMMIT 2 DB-->>API: Changes persisted end API-->>UI: Interview response with display names UI->>API: Reload recruiter workspace datasets API-->>UI: Updated applicants, interviews and totals UI-->>R: Updated applicant list and interview schedule Note over API,DB: Two separate commits.
Foreign keys validate IDs,
not recruiter ownership.
notes: Successful authentication and database writes are assumed; failures return before later steps.
The recruiter role dependency is implemented, but schedule_interview does not verify ownership of the submitted application. The diagram records this gap rather than inventing a check.
Interview persistence precedes the application status/notification commit. The meeting link is supplied data; there is no video-conferencing integration.

title: Application submission activity
subtitle: Guarded branches for internal/external roles and the internal API processing path.
notes: Filled circle: initial node. Bullseye: activity final. Rounded rectangles: actions. Diamonds: decisions. Every outgoing decision edge has a guard.
External applications redirect to a supplied company link; this branch does not create a local application record.
The internal branch assumes a valid active-account token. A rejected request ends this attempt; a user may start another attempt.
Application validation does not currently enforce active-post or deadline eligibility; no such checks are invented here.
